verification.method: Adversarial verification. Each cited file and line range was opened and checked against src/architecture_tests.rs (domain_and_services_do_not_reach_into_storage, background_layers_hold_no_gtk_or_ui (bans gtk4/adw/glib/gio/crate::ui in controller/storage/obs), only_the_obs_adapter_imports_obws, domain_types_depend_on_neither_gtk_nor_obs) and against the CLAUDE.md threading rules. Third-party claims were checked in ~/.cargo/registry sources: obws-0.15.0 Cargo.toml and client/mod.rs, serde-saphyr-2.1.1 de/budget.rs and de/options.rs. This is a self-review with no fresh-context subagent, and nothing was run natively.

summary:
The security reviewer's trust-boundary pass mostly holds up.

Confirmed:
- Pango markup injection through the StatusPage description in mixer.rs and Toast::new in window.rs. This is a realistic bug: a scene named 'Q&A' blanks the label.
- ws:// only. The obws `tls` feature is not enabled, and there is no non-loopback warning.
- The plaintext password sits in the Debug+Clone AppState.
- Startup blocks on a keyring call that is joined before GTK starts.
- Two keyring ports. The connect race is PLAUSIBLE but not reproduced.
- Lossy config downgrade.
- The deny.toml exception expires 2026-11-20 (today is 2026-11-14).
- The obs/ to controller::event::ConnectionInfo inversion.
- Stringly-typed AppError.
- Endpoint and paths included in exports.

Adjusted:
- security-07: the screenshot is dead code. Every production caller of ui::workspace::request passes screenshot=false (ui/workspace.rs:179, 291), so it is never fetched. This is a YAGNI deletion, not a live memory risk.
- security-03: the line numbers are wrong. storage/config/connections.rs has only 179 lines, save_connection is at 61 and the format! at 43. 'Injection' is overstated because the host is typed by the local user. Duplicated identity formatting, IPv6 brackets and alias splitting are real.
- security-11: serde-saphyr's default budget already caps events at 1M and nodes at 250k, and enforces an alias/anchor ratio. The import runs off the UI thread via background_io::run.
- security-15: glib is banned in storage/ by architecture_tests::background_layers_hold_no_gtk_or_ui, so the glib::user_config_dir fix would fail tests. Use std::env::home_dir instead.
- security-14: CustomCssPreference is a domain serde type. A storage deserialize_with referencing storage::xdg from domain would break domain_and_services_do_not_reach_into_storage.
- security-16: the domain-to-storage ban already exists. Only the controller ban for obs/storage/domain/services is new.
- security-12: raised to medium urgency because of the CI cliff in 6 days.
- security-08: lowered to low.

Refuted inside the splits:
- The registry split step that moves behaviour 'into the domain module as free functions over &mut SceneRegistry' would break the architecture test, because domain/ cannot name a storage type. Rewritten.
- The obs/client.rs split claim that 'pub(super) fields are already visible' is only partly true: only `inner` is pub(super). Child modules under client/ still see private fields, but siblings do not.

findings.title: OBS-controlled scene names and error text are rendered as Pango markup in StatusPage descriptions and Toast titles
findings.evidence: mixer.rs:798-806 passes the description straight to StatusPage::builder().description(). Callers interpolate the OBS scene name (736-746 with scene_label, 937 with scene). 808-823 interpolates scene and the OBS error message. graph.rs:81 and inventory.rs:340 do escape with glib::markup_escape_text. window.rs uses adw::Toast::new(&message) at 681, 777, 886, 971, 1342 and 1424, and Toast::builder().title(fl!(.., error = message)) at 1137-1145, all with OBS or network-derived text. Cargo.toml:8 enables libadwaita v1_4. Other toasts and rows in the codebase already call .use_markup(false), for example quick_actions.rs:21, health_alerts.rs:21, preflight.rs:51 and settings/connections.rs:291. That makes window.rs and mixer.rs the inconsistent outliers.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add src/ui/markup.rs with `pub(crate) fn escape(s: &str) -> glib::GString` and `pub(crate) fn plain_toast(title: impl AsRef) -> adw::Toast`, which builds with .use_markup(false). 2) AdwStatusPage:description has no use-markup property, so escape in append_mixer_status and append_mixer_error_status: `.description(markup::escape(description))`. 3) Replace each Toast::new and Toast::builder() in window.rs (681, 777, 886, 971, 1137, 1342, 1424) and hotkeys.rs:93 with plain_toast. 4) Add an architecture test using the existing scanner, e.g. violations("ui", &["adw::Toast::new"], &["ui/markup.rs"]). Don't write a new syn visitor for the StatusPage argument check: grep-style tests can't prove an argument is escaped, so handle StatusPage in review. 5) Add a pure test that markup::escape("x & y") round-trips, and a native test in the tools/test-native.py lane only if cheap.
findings.risk: A scene named 'Q&A' or 'A & B' blanks the mixer status label, toast text can be spoofed, and operator alerts disappear.
findings.verifier_note: Every cited line was read and matches. Toast use-markup defaults to TRUE in libadwaita >= 1.4. The existing .use_markup(false) builder calls show the API is available with v1_4. The rule against non-escaped StatusPage descriptions can't be enforced reliably with the token scanner, so step 4 is narrowed to forbidding Toast::new.

findings.title: OBS WebSocket is plaintext ws:// only, with no TLS option and no non-loopback warning
findings.evidence: client.rs:76-87 builds ConnectConfig without `tls`, and Cargo.toml:20 is `obws = { version = "0.15", features = ["events"] }`. In obws-0.15.0/src/client/mod.rs:220-229, tls() returns false without the feature, and at 278-283 it formats "{}://{}:{}" with ws/wss. A grep of src/ for loopback, wss or tls finds only test fixtures.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add a pure `domain::connection::endpoint::is_loopback(&ObsHost) -> bool` (no GTK) and show a persistent warning row in ui/pages/settings/connections.rs when the host is not loopback. Add the new i18n key settings-connection-unencrypted-remote to every locale. 2) Add a docs/obs-websocket.md and docs/user-guide.md note: obs-websocket itself serves plain ws, so remote use needs an SSH tunnel or a TLS reverse proxy. 3) Only then optionally enable the obws `tls` feature and add Transport::{Ws,Wss} to the endpoint. That feature pulls in tokio-websockets/rustls and webpki-roots, so first run `cargo deny check licenses bans` (webpki-roots license, ring/aws-lc) and get a maintainer decision.
findings.risk: Remote OBS setups leak a crackable auth exchange and allow on-path control of a live stream.
findings.verifier_note: The facts are confirmed against the obws source. The order is changed: warning plus docs first (cheap, no new deps), TLS second, because the feature adds a rustls dependency tree that must pass deny.toml. OBS has no native wss, so the Wss transport only helps behind a proxy. The proposed 'tokio-websockets server test' is replaced by a pure uri/is_loopback unit test.

findings.lines: 99-105 (ObsConfig), 358 (legacy_registry_endpoint format); src/storage/config/connections.rs 43 (legacy endpoint format), 61-86 (save_connection); src/obs/client.rs 99; src/controller/state.rs 788-796 (workflow_scope); src/storage/show_workspaces.rs 10-15 (WorkspaceKey); src/ui/pages/settings/connections.rs 186-215 (save_fields)
findings.title: OBS endpoint is a raw host String, and `host:port` text is formatted in five places and used as workspace identity (primitive obsession)
findings.evidence: ObsConfig { host: String, port: u16 }. save_connection (connections.rs:61-68) rejects only an empty host or port 0, and save_fields only trims. Identity strings are built independently at client.rs:99, connections.rs:43, config.rs:358 and state.rs:793 (`format!("{}:{}", host, port)`). That string flows into ScopeBinding.endpoint and WorkspaceKey.endpoint. obws formats the raw host into the URI (obws client/mod.rs 278-283), so an IPv6 literal without brackets fails to parse, and aliases (LOCALHOST, 127.0.0.1, a trailing dot) produce separate workspaces. client.rs:100 also hard-codes connection_id "default" until with_connection_id is called.
findings.recommendation:
Create src/domain/connection/{mod.rs,endpoint.rs}:
- `ObsHost`: an Ip(IpAddr) or a lowercase Dns(String) with the trailing dot stripped, rejecting `/ @ ? # [ ] :` and whitespace.
- `ObsEndpoint { host, port: NonZeroU16 }`, with FromStr/Display. Display brackets IPv6.
- `EndpointKey(String)`, produced by `ObsEndpoint::key()`.

Replace the four format! sites with `endpoint.key()`. Keep ObsConfig's JSON shape: validate in storage via `#[serde(try_from = "RawObsConfig")]`, or validate post-load in `apply_migrations` so an invalid stored host becomes a startup notice rather than a hard parse failure.

Do NOT canonicalise existing keys in show-workspaces.json in the first PR. `legacy_owner` and `legacy_registry_endpoint` adoption compare exact strings, and rewriting them can silently orphan curation. If you do canonicalise, add a migration test that loads an old-key store and proves the same entry is selected.

Tests: a table test in endpoint.rs (IPv6, case, trailing dot, the reject list), a config round-trip test, and a key-equality test.
findings.risk: Broken IPv6 support, duplicated curation per alias, and identity logic that drifts across 4 sites.
findings.verifier_note: The cited lines were wrong: connections.rs is 179 lines, so 374-399 and 355-356 don't exist. The real sites are connections.rs:43 and 61, config.rs:358, and a fourth at state.rs:793 that the reviewer missed. 'Injection' is downgraded because the host comes from the local user's own input or config, not from a remote party. The remaining issues are correctness and primitive obsession. Placing ObsEndpoint in domain/ is architecture-safe, since storage and obs may import domain.

findings.title: Plaintext OBS password cached in the shared Debug+Clone AppState for the whole process lifetime
findings.evidence: Confirmed at state.rs:437-438 and 456. Readers and writers are settings/connections.rs:113, 121, 146, 156, 249 and 382. The controller re-reads the keyring itself (session_controller.rs:270-273), so it does not need this copy. No current code formats the whole AppState: tests at state.rs:2851 and 2855 format only state.config and state.registry. The risk is latent.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add src/domain/connection/credential.rs: `pub struct ObsPassword(Box<str>)` with a manual Debug (`ObsPassword(***)`), no Display, and `expose()`. Defer zeroize until deny.toml review. 2) Remove AppState::obs_password and StartupData.password. 3) Make the settings Editor own `Option<ObsPassword>`, and type PasswordWrites.confirmed (settings.rs:457-460) as `Option<ObsPassword>`. 4) Have storage/secret.rs return and accept ObsPassword. 5) Add a unit test that the Debug output does not contain the secret. Skip the proposed name-based architecture test, because the token scanner can't check field names cheaply.
findings.risk: Secret disclosure through any future Debug of AppState or panic output.
findings.verifier_note: Code confirmed. Severity stays medium, but note that no current Debug print of AppState exists. The architecture test for field names is dropped as impractical with the existing path scanner.

findings.title: Startup blocks GTK initialisation on a synchronous Secret Service call, and the keyring is touched on every launch
findings.evidence: app.rs:42-48 calls secret::get_obs_password inside the startup thread, and 61 joins it before adw::Application is built. The value is used only by the settings editor cache (connections.rs:113).
findings.recommendation: Delete the keyring read and StartupData.password from app.rs. In ui/pages/settings/connections.rs, call `editor.load_password(id, generation)` (already at 133-163, on SerialLane::Secret) when the editor is first built, with busy(true), instead of reading state.obs_password at refresh_fields:112-114. To prove startup never touches the keyring there must be a seam, because startup calls secret:: directly. Extract `fn load_startup(read: impl StartupReaders) -> StartupData`, or simply assert in a test that StartupData has no password field (the deletion is enough). The window.rs:2375 panicking-provider pattern applies to ControllerDependencies, not to app.rs startup.
findings.risk: The app looks hung on a locked or wedged keyring, and users get needless unlock prompts.
findings.verifier_note: The issue is confirmed. The recommendation's test was not executable as written: startup has no ObsPasswordProvider seam, because it calls storage::secret directly. The editor also does not currently lazy-load on first build; load_password runs only from change_selection (connections.rs:117-131), so first-build loading must be added.

findings.title: Two uncoordinated keyring ports; Connect can read a stale password while a Secret-lane write is still queued (PLAUSIBLE, not reproduced)
findings.evidence: save_password submits on SerialLane::Secret (settings.rs:479-481). connect() (255-275) waits only for the Config barrier (persist_config_with) and then dispatches AppCommand::Connect. The controller reads the keyring on Tokio's blocking pool (session_controller.rs:270-273), outside the Secret lane. save_password does not set busy(true), so the Connect button stays clickable during the write.
findings.recommendation: 1) Define a single port, `domain::connection::credential::CredentialStore` (sync, Send+Sync; called only from the blocking pool or the Secret lane). 2) Implement it once in storage/secret.rs as KeyringCredentialStore. 3) Inject the same Arc<dyn CredentialStore> into ControllerDependencies and the settings editor, and delete ConnectionSecrets and ObsPasswordProvider. 4) In connect(), dispatch Connect from the completion of a no-op `run_serialized(SerialLane::Secret, || (), ..)` started inside the Config barrier's completion. Lanes are FIFO, so every prior secret write lands first. 5) Add a pure test that Secret-lane ordering delivers the no-op after a queued write (background_io tests already cover FIFO ordering), plus the native editor test.
findings.risk: Intermittent auth failures right after a password change, and duplicated credential paths drift apart.
findings.verifier_note: The race is plausible from the code; it was not reproduced. The Secret lane is a FIFO SerialQueue (background_io.rs:19-46), so the barrier fix is sound. A CredentialStore trait in domain/ does not violate architecture_tests: it holds no GTK or storage references.

findings.title: OBS screenshot request path is dead: never requested in production, yet kept in AppState and the obs adapter
findings.evidence: The only production callers of ui::workspace::request pass screenshot=false: refresh at ui/workspace.rs:179 and act_expected at 291. operating_panel.rs:150 and the controller tests also set false. The 960x540 TakeScreenshot is therefore never sent. WorkspaceState.screenshot, screenshot_scene and screenshot_observed_at are written only in event_reconciliation.rs and cleared in state.rs:379-381 and ui/workspace.rs:201, and no reader displays them.
findings.recommendation: Delete (YAGNI): WorkspaceRequest.screenshot, ObservedWorkspace.screenshot, ObsClient::get_source_screenshot and source_screenshot (keep source_screenshot only if get_scene_thumbnail uses it; check client.rs:577-597 first), the WorkspaceState screenshot* fields, and the related reconciliation branches and tests (event_reconciliation.rs:438-454, state.rs:2621-2623, 2697-2698, 2875). If a feature later needs it, decode in obs/ through a bounded PNG value object that shares ui/previews.rs bounded_png rules.
findings.risk: Dead state in a god struct and misleading reads in reviews. There is no live memory risk today.
findings.verifier_note: The claim that the screenshot is 'fetched ... on every workspace refresh' is false: every production path passes screenshot=false. Recategorised from performance/medium to dead-code/low. The deletion recommendation stands.

findings.title: Show-workspace store grows without bound, keyed by OBS-supplied collection names; past 8 MiB every read and write fails
findings.evidence: Confirmed: load_or_create pushes a new entry for each unseen key and never evicts, validate has no count cap, and both read_store and write_store enforce REGISTRY_LIMIT (8 MiB, small_file.rs:10). Once the cap is crossed, read_store also fails, not only writes.
findings.recommendation: Add `last_used_unix_ms: u64` (serde default 0) to StoredWorkspace, updated on load_or_create hits as part of the next write rather than as an extra write on every read. Add MAX_WORKSPACES = 64 with LRU eviction that never evicts the target or legacy_owner, and surface the eviction to the UI. Tests: MAX+1 evicts the oldest; the active entry and legacy_owner survive.
findings.risk: Persistence loss after long-term use with many collections or endpoints.
findings.verifier_note: The code is confirmed. Severity is lowered from medium to low: an empty registry serialises to well under 1 KiB, so reaching 8 MiB needs thousands of collections or very large registries. A hostile OBS must also be connected to repeatedly while switching collections. Line ranges are corrected.

findings.title: A newer config is silently down-converted: unknown fields are dropped on the next save, and even on read
findings.evidence: migrate (326-334) only warns when version > CURRENT_VERSION (5). AppConfig has no flatten or capture field. Separately, apply_migrations (317-323) returns true when migrate_legacy_custom_css_path changes something, even for a newer-version config, so read_config_from_path (238-240) rewrites a newer file and drops its unknown keys at read time, without any user save.
findings.recommendation: Prefer option (b): refuse to write when version > CURRENT_VERSION. Return io::ErrorKind::Unsupported from write_config_to_path, skip the read-time rewrite for newer configs, and add ConfigStartupNotice::NewerVersion. Option (a), `#[serde(flatten)] extra: serde_json::Map`, interacts badly with existing `skip_serializing` and `rename` fields (legacy_theme_mode, the legacy css path). Tests: a version-99 file with an unknown key is unchanged on disk after read; a save is refused.
findings.risk: Data loss on downgrade or rollback.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed. Added that the read path also rewrites newer configs when custom-css migration fires. Option (b) is recommended over the flatten approach.

findings.title: `read_config_from_path` has a write side effect and swallows its error
findings.evidence: config.rs:238-240: `if apply_migrations(&mut config) { let _ = write_config_to_path(path, &config); }`. It runs in the app.rs startup thread before any GTK lane exists.
findings.recommendation: Add `needs_persist: bool` to LoadedConfig and keep read_config_from_path pure. After GTK starts, app.rs (build_ui path, around line 439) calls ui::persist::persist_config(nav, |_| {}) when needs_persist is set, so a failure reaches the close-guard accounting and the UI. Test: reading a legacy file leaves the bytes on disk unchanged.
findings.verifier_note: The CQS violation and the swallowed error are confirmed. The 'outside the ordered SerialLane::Config' framing is weak: the write happens before any lane job can be submitted, so there is no ordering race. The real defect is the swallowed error. The recommendation is kept.

findings.title: YAML import relies on serde-saphyr's default budget and has no semantic count or length caps
findings.evidence: registry.rs:658 calls serde_saphyr::from_str. serde-saphyr-2.1.1 de/budget.rs:277-305 defaults: max_events 1_000_000, max_nodes 250_000, max_aliases 50_000, enforce_alias_anchor_ratio true (min 100, x10), max_recorded_anchor_bytes 64 MiB, max_depth 64. Input is capped at 8 MiB (small_file.rs:11). The import runs through background_io::run (persist.rs:416-426), not on the GTK thread. There are no count or length caps on scenes, decks or presets.
findings.recommendation: In the new storage/registry/import.rs, use `serde_saphyr::from_str_with_options` (de/api.rs:135) with `Options { budget: Some(Budget { max_aliases: 1_000, max_anchors: 1_000, max_recorded_anchor_bytes: 1 << 20, max_nodes: 100_000, max_merge_keys: 100, ..Budget::default() }), ..Options::default() }`. Then call `validate_import(&SceneRegistry) -> Result<(), ImportError>` with caps such as 2_000 scenes, 200 decks and 512-byte strings. Tests: a billion-laughs fixture is rejected; an oversized deck map is rejected.
findings.risk: Bounded CPU and memory spike on a crafted show file (seconds, not unbounded), and UI curation flooded with junk entries.
findings.verifier_note: The API names were verified to exist. The risk is downgraded: the defaults already bound expansion (1M events, alias/anchor ratio), and the parse runs on a background thread, so 'UI-thread stall' is wrong. Tightening is still cheap defence in depth.

findings.title: RUSTSEC-2026-0374 exception expires 2026-11-20 (6 days from 2026-11-14); CI fails every build after that
findings.evidence: deny.toml:7 has the expiry. .github/workflows/ci.yml:137-138 runs tools/check-advisory-exceptions.py, and 150-154 run cargo audit and cargo deny. Cargo.lock:208 has basic-toml and :1249-1254 has i18n-config 0.4.8, which depends on it.
findings.recommendation: Do this before 2026-11-20. Check for an i18n-config release that drops basic-toml 0.1.10 (cargo-i18n PR #176). If one exists, run `cargo update -p i18n-config` and remove the ignore. If not, renew the expiry with the same reachability note in a separate `build:` commit. Do not widen the ignore.
findings.risk: CI breaks and blocks all merges and releases.
findings.verifier_note: The facts are confirmed. Severity is raised from low to medium because it is time-critical: it must be the first task an implementer picks up.

findings.title: `background_io::run` spawns an OS thread per call and polls the result every 20 ms
findings.evidence: Confirmed at 105-109 (std::thread::spawn) and 357 (timeout_add_local 20 ms). gio::spawn_blocking is already used in ui/global_shortcuts/portal.rs:68, so the replacement API is in the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Reimplement run on `gio::spawn_blocking` plus `glib::MainContext::default().spawn_local`. Keep PendingJob accounting (288-304), because flush_pending (318) depends on it, and call record_failure on a JoinError. Keep SerialQueue lanes on their own threads, and do not move the Secret lane to the GIO pool: a hung keyring would occupy a shared pool thread. Replace polling in the lane delivery with an async channel awaited through spawn_local. Existing tests at 406-894 guard the ordering.
findings.risk: Thread bursts on repeated user actions, and 20 ms wakeups.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed. Added constraints: preserve PendingJob/flush_pending semantics, and keep keyring work off the shared GIO pool. Impact is low because calls are driven by user clicks.

findings.title: Custom CSS paths may be relative and are resolved against the process working directory
findings.evidence: CustomCssPreference { light_path, dark_path: Option<PathBuf> } is a serde type in domain/. theme.rs:193-197 reads the path unchanged through small_file::read_to_string. validate_custom_css (theme.rs:279-307) blocks @import and url(). Paths chosen in the file chooser are absolute, so only a hand-edited config.json produces a relative path.
findings.recommendation: Do not put a deserialize_with that references storage::xdg on the domain type: domain/ cannot depend on storage/ (architecture_tests::domain_and_services_do_not_reach_into_storage). Instead, either (a) reject a non-absolute path in ThemeManager::load_custom_css, returning CustomCssLoad::Failed with a localised message, or (b) normalise in storage::config::apply_migrations by dropping non-absolute paths with a startup notice. A StylesheetPath value object in domain is fine if its constructor only checks is_absolute(). Test: a relative path is rejected.
findings.risk: An unexpected stylesheet is loaded depending on the launch CWD. Self-inflicted only.
findings.verifier_note: The struct is named CustomCssPreference, not CustomCss. The proposed storage-layer deserializer is impossible without a storage DTO, because the serde type lives in domain/. The fix is re-placed so it does not break architecture_tests.

findings.title: XDG resolution falls back to the current directory when HOME is unset, and accepts relative XDG_* values
findings.evidence: Both functions end with `.unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."))`. A relative XDG_CONFIG_HOME or XDG_STATE_HOME is accepted, though the XDG spec says to ignore it. The resolution logic is duplicated between the two functions (DRY).
findings.recommendation: Write one private `fn base_dir(var: &str, home_suffix: &str) -> Option<PathBuf>`. It ignores non-absolute XDG values and falls back to std::env::home_dir(), which is stable and undeprecated on the pinned toolchain and consults getpwuid when HOME is unset. Return None instead of '.', and have callers run with in-memory defaults plus a startup notice. Do NOT use glib::user_config_dir: architecture_tests::background_layers_hold_no_gtk_or_ui bans `glib::` in src/storage/. Test in a child process (background_io::isolated_test_child pattern) with HOME and XDG_* unset or relative.
findings.risk: Settings read from or written to an unexpected shared location.
findings.verifier_note: The issue is confirmed. The original glib fix would fail architecture_tests (storage bans glib::). Replaced with std::env::home_dir, and the relative-XDG handling and DRY note were added.

findings.title: Anti-corruption layer is inverted: obs/ imports `controller::event::ConnectionInfo`
findings.evidence: Confirmed at client.rs:14 and mapper.rs:12. A grep of obs/, storage/, domain/ and services/ for crate::controller or crate::ui finds only these two, plus a test-only use at storage/bookmarks.rs:89 (unix_ms inside #[cfg(test)]). architecture_tests already bans domain to storage (domain_and_services_do_not_reach_into_storage) and crate::ui in controller, storage and obs (background_layers_hold_no_gtk_or_ui).
findings.recommendation: 1) Move ConnectionInfo as-is (String fields) to src/domain/connection/info.rs, and `pub use` it from controller/event.rs so call sites are unchanged. Do not couple this to security-03. Switch the fields to ObsEndpoint and ConnectionId later. 2) Add one architecture test: violations for obs, storage, domain and services against ["crate::controller"]. The test-only bookmarks use is already exempt from the scanner, but move `unix_ms` to src/infra/clock.rs anyway, because controller/workspace.rs is the wrong owner. 3) Do NOT add a new domain-to-storage test; it already exists.
findings.verifier_note: The core finding is confirmed. Dropped the duplicate domain-to-storage test and removed the false dependency on security-03, so the move can land first.

findings.title: Stringly-typed AppError erases the credential and auth failure kind
findings.evidence: Confirmed: Connection(String), Request(String) and Storage(String) via to_string(). storage/secret.rs:33-54 maps every non-NoEntry keyring error to AppError::storage. infra/error.rs also renders fl! (54+), which mixes a presentation concern into infra.
findings.recommendation: Add AppError::Credential(CredentialError { Locked, Unavailable, NotFound, Backend(String) }), mapped from keyring::Error in storage/secret.rs, and AppError::Auth mapped from the obws auth error in obs/client.rs connect, so obws types stay in obs/. Localise each variant. Unit test the mapping table. A later step is to move user_message rendering into ui/ (an error_text.rs) so infra stops calling fl!.
findings.risk: Poor diagnostics and recovery paths that can't be tested.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed. Added an optional note about separating user_message from infra.

findings.title: Session report exports always include endpoint, connection name and OBS host paths
findings.evidence: Confirmed: the metadata JSON at 87-91 includes connection_id, endpoint and connection_name. The obs_host_path column is at 73. The JSON export serialises the whole ReportDocument.
findings.recommendation: Add `ExportOptions { redact_endpoint, redact_paths }` to report_export::write, with a toggle in the session_reports export dialog. New i18n keys go in every locale. Whether redaction is on by default is a product decision, because support workflows may need the endpoint. Recommend default off with a visible checkbox, or ask the maintainer. Test: the redacted CSV has no host:port and no '/' in path cells.
findings.risk: Accidental infrastructure disclosure in shared reports.
findings.verifier_note: Confirmed. The default-on redaction is flagged as a product decision instead of a security requirement.

findings.title: SceneRegistry is a storage serde struct acting as a god aggregate across several bounded contexts
findings.evidence: Confirmed: 12 fields spanning curation, decks, bindings, quick actions, audio alerts, presets, inputs and rules. state.rs:454 has `pub registry: SceneRegistry`. Partial anti-corruption already exists: domain::registry::{SceneRegistrySnapshot, SceneMetadata, GraphDependencyPolicy} (registry.rs:17), and most field element types are already domain types (domain::action_shortcut::ActionBinding, operator_action::OperatorPin, health::AudioRule, audio_preset::AudioPreset). storage/registry/ already contains decks.rs and identity.rs submodules. The import neutraliser (662-677) hard-codes the field list.
findings.recommendation:
Phase 0: add a golden JSON and YAML shape test, plus an import-policy test that enumerates every Vec or Map field and fails when a new one is added without a neutralisation decision.
Phase 1 (storage-internal, no architecture risk): split storage/registry.rs into registry/{dto.rs, io.rs, import.rs, curation.rs}, keeping the decks.rs and identity.rs that already exist.
Phase 2: introduce domain aggregates. `domain/registry/` becomes a directory holding `scene_catalog.rs`, `decks.rs` and `show_curation.rs` (the aggregate root). Bindings go to domain/operator_action.rs or a new domain/operator/bindings.rs. Graph rules go next to domain::registry::GraphDependencyPolicy. Reuse the existing `domain::registry` name, which is already the ubiquitous term, instead of a new `curation` namespace.
Phase 3: storage/registry/dto.rs implements From<SceneRegistryDto> for ShowCuration and the reverse.
Phase 4: AppState holds ShowCuration. Each neutralisation rule becomes a domain method (e.g. `OperatorBindings::disable_all()`), called from storage/registry/import.rs.
Behaviour must not move into domain/ while it still operates on the storage SceneRegistry type, because domain cannot import storage.
findings.risk: Every curation feature touches one type, and import policy can silently miss new fields.
findings.smell: Large Class, Divergent Change, Shotgun Surgery
findings.verifier_note: The god-struct diagnosis is confirmed. Adjusted to reuse the existing domain::registry module and the existing storage/registry/{decks,identity}.rs, and to state the architecture constraint (domain cannot name storage types) that fixes the phase order.

proposed_splits.order: 1) Move the tests out. Keep `pub(crate) mod control_tests` declared in client.rs, because src/controller/workspace/audio_presets/tests.rs:2 and src/obs/regression_tests.rs:4 import mock_client by path. 2) Extract media.rs. 3) Extract controls.rs. 4) Extract queries.rs and outputs.rs as child modules (`mod queries;` inside client.rs). Children can see ObsClient's private fields (requests, images, endpoint, connection_id). Making them siblings like the existing obs/audio.rs and obs/sources.rs would require raising those fields to pub(super); only `inner` is pub(super) today (client.rs:54). 5) Only then change the connect signature (security-03/04). proposed_splits.safety_net: Existing loopback tests, control_tests and obs/regression_tests.rs. Add a password handshake test against obs_fixture before step 5.
proposed_splits.verifier_note: The structure and line ranges match. The claim 'pub(super) fields are already visible' is corrected: only `inner` is pub(super), and the child-module placement is what makes private fields visible. Added the external control_tests import paths that must be preserved. There is a precedent sibling pattern (obs/audio.rs, sources.rs, scene_activation.rs, operator_inputs.rs, audio_presets.rs as `impl ObsClient` blocks), so implementers may instead pick siblings and raise visibility; either choice works, but stay consistent.
